reviews.text: Excellent service from arrival to departure. Dr. Castro, as always, was very professional, and her assistants were very caring with the pets. Thank you. I've attached a photo of my pet, Tina.

Generally they do a great job but unfortunately I was disappointed with the grooming of my cat this time (my second time getting her groomed here). She looks nothing like the picture I provided, the haircut was choppy and they shaved her tail when I specifically requested they leave it fluffy. I am not sure if they have a new groomer or what. Although they gave me a discount, I would've much preferred to pay full price for a job well done. Specifically for grooming services, I advise making sure that what you want is clearly understood by staff (front desk and the groomer) to avoid them taking liberties.

Other than that, all other services I have experienced (vaccines, surgeries, communication on the health, status and care) have been stellar.

I recently brought my senior dog to this clinic after she became very sick. I called on a Thursday and was told they only take appointments which was fine and they were able to get her in for Friday at noon.

What I didn’t expect was a $50 upfront fee just to book the appointment. I was told it would go toward the $48 visit fee, but still that wasn’t mentioned over the phone, and it felt a bit sneaky. I was told this has been their policy for about a year.

During the visit, the vet recommended full blood work because of my dog’s age to check liver, kidney, and pancreas function. I understood the reasoning, but I was shocked when the nurse brought out an invoice for $565 just for the blood work, with an additional medications fee costing $240($800total) if I chose to treat it as an upset stomach instead. And that’s before any actual treatment. I’ve heard that the clinic was taken over by a corporate company, and that’s when the prices started going up. I already knew the previous owners had sold it they were fair, cared about their clients, and didn’t feel like they were trying to squeeze every dollar out of you. Now? It feels more like a business than a place of care. And for the neighborhood this clinic is in, these new prices just don’t make sense. It’s completely out of step with the community. Unfortunately, I’ll be taking my pet elsewhere moving forward. I need a vet that’s both compassionate and reasonable not one that feels like it’s been taken over by corporate profit goals.

⭐☆☆☆☆ – If I could give zero stars, I would.

The only reason this place even gets one star is because Google won’t allow zero. My experience with Long Drive Dog & Cat Hospital was one of the most frustrating and heartbreaking veterinary visits I’ve ever had.

When I first called, the staff sounded friendly and confident. They told me prescriptions were “not expensive, usually $20–$60,” and that as a first-time client I’d need to leave a $50 deposit that would go toward the visit. That was the only part that turned out to be true.

When I arrived, the same employees who quoted me prices over the phone suddenly acted like they had no idea what anything cost. I literally watched them answering calls and giving estimates to other customers, yet when I asked about prices, they said, “You’ll have to ask the vet.”

Then came the exam. My ten-year-old dog, about 48 pounds and clearly in pain with swollen mammary glands, was made to climb onto a tall metal scale nearly four feet off the ground—no ramp, no low option, nothing to make it easier for an older, hurting dog. I had to lift her myself while she trembled. The exam table was just as bad: slick, cold metal where she could barely keep her footing.

The first assistant asked a few questions and left. The veterinarian came in, gave a quick glance, said she was swollen, ignored the other glands I mentioned, and when I asked about the cost he gave a vague, dismissive answer—something like, “Someone will bring that for you.” Then he simply walked out of the room and never came back.

Moments later, two completely different women—neither of whom I had met before—walked in holding a bill for over $200 for the same two antibiotics another clinic charged me about $40 total for. They also tried to add a rabies shot even after I told them she was fully vaccinated.

At that point I was furious. There were three other customers in the lobby about to be called back, and I spoke loud enough for them to hear what had happened so they could think twice before trusting this place. The whole operation felt like bait-and-switch entrapment—offer low prices over the phone, take a deposit, then surprise you with inflated charges once your pet is already there.

I left angry, heartbroken, and completely disillusioned. My senior dog deserved compassion and honest care, not confusion and manipulation.
If you truly care about your pet’s wellbeing, stay far away from this clinic. They value profit over compassion every single time.
